articles.image_title: Energiekrise in Asien: HAGONOY, PHILIPPINES - MARCH 09: A fisherman buys fuel at a riverside gas station a day before a major fuel price surge caused by the U.S./Israel intervention in Iran takes effect, on March 09, 2026 in Hagonoy, Bulacan province, Philippines. The Philippines is among the worst affected in Asia by global oil price shocks, where a decades-old oil deregulation law allows fuel companies to quickly pass price spikes to consumers. With about 90% of its oil sourced from the Middle East and little strategic reserves, disruptions quickly drive up transport costs, inflation, and the price of basic goods. (Photo by Ezra Acayan/Getty Images)
